subject: Geopolitics
title: The Responsibility to Protect
description: One-minute skill: The Responsibility to Protect.

hook.text: After Rwanda's genocide, the world asked: should nations intervene to stop mass atrocities even without permission?

buildup.text: In 2005, the UN adopted R2P: if a state fails to protect its people, the international community should step up.

discovery.text: R2P was invoked in Libya in 2011 to justify NATO airstrikes. The intervention toppled Gaddafi but created new chaos.

twist.text: Russia and China now block R2P in the Security Council, citing Libya as proof that intervention masks regime change.

climax.text: R2P is a powerful idea weakened by selective application.

punchline.text: The duty to protect exists. The will is selective.

quiz.question: Why do Russia and China often block R2P in the UN?
options: They believe no state ever threatens its own people
They view it as cover for Western regime change
They want to lead interventions themselves
